prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1012; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
At approximately the time noted in the report header, Driver 1 was traveling through the intersection in Baytown, Texas, when the front of Driver 2's vehicle struck the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 reported neck pain consistent with whiplash and stated that the force of the collision threw them forward against the restraint. The injury described fits the type and force of this impact.

Damage to both vehicles is largely consistent with a side impact at this angle. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the general location of the damage. A few older scratches on the lower rear quarter panel of Driver 1's vehicle may predate this collision; the examining officer noted them but could not link them to this event.

No independent witnesses were located. Responding officers and two people at the scene confirmed that Driver 1 and Passenger were inside the vehicle when it came to rest. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle, according to documents presented at the scene.
